newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir wants "accurate" reporting on Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir wants "accurate" reporting on Malaysia.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday he wanted to see more "accurate" media reporting on Malaysia, saying it would do a disservice to people otherwise.
"Yes we do make mistakes in Malaysia, we sometimes do wrong things here, but they must be reported in the proper perspective," Mahathir said.

At the opening of the bureau of Japan's Nikkei newspaper, Mahathir said Malaysia was often described by the media as ready to break out into racial violence due to the "incompatibility" of its multi-racial, multi-lingual and multi-religious population.
Malaysia has about 20 million people, over half of whom are Bumiputera (ethnic Malay), about a third Chinese and the rest Indians and other minorities.
"But yet Malaysia today is one country where we manage to live and work together," Mahathir said. "Malaysia's economic performance is actually the result of political stability in the country."
He said the Western media also often liked to say that his government controlled the press.
"I would like to point out that those who said this have never bothered to read the vernacular papers which have nothing good to say about this government, at least some of them," he said.
In 1988, Mahathir's government suspended the operations of several local newspapers after finding them responsible for inciting racial disharmony.
Mahathir said accurate information was important because people relied on it when making decisions.

"Investors need to have information before they can invest. Traders need information before they can do any trade with any country. Any information is much more important of course if it is accurate," he said.
Mahathir said he has found it a common practice for the media to publish or transmit sensational and negative reports which attract more readers and subscribers.

"Newspapers and the media often condemned governments for misuse of power and for abuse of power or corruption but is it not corruption and an abuse of power to do something you know very well is wrong simply because you, the media, have power," he said.
